answer:
Verdict: no

## Scheduling over the whole trace (0–30,687.680 ms)

The sampler was preempted only 5 times, for 0.013 ms total; its longest preemption was 0.003 ms. After waking, it waited to run 14,985 times, but the median wait was 0.005 ms. Its total time waiting for a CPU was 134.585 ms—0.4% of its lifetime.

The largest identified CPU holder during those waits was ticker’s **maintenance** thread (TID 629355), at 22.0%; **uploader** (TID 629354) accounted for 13.9%. Most of the waiting time was when the CPU was idle or handling interrupts (60.0%). The holder attribution is low confidence, so those threads are likely contributors, not a certain cause. Interrupt handling itself was low: at most 0.025% of CPU 3 in the measured stretch.

So there were some short scheduling delays, including one 29.597 ms wait, but the trace does not show the sampler being repeatedly interrupted by higher-priority work.
